facts.material: 23 AWG copper conductors insulated with FEP, four twisted pairs, low-smoke flame-retardant PVC jacket
facts.form: bulk cable on reels, not fitted with connectors; rated voltage 48 V
facts.end_use: telecommunications/data networks in buildings (plenum, vertical, horizontal, backbone)

gri_path: GRI 1: heading 8544 insulated electric conductors; not coaxial (8544.20), not fitted with connectors (so not 8544.42)
GRI 6: 8544.49 other electric conductors for a voltage not exceeding 1,000 V, not fitted with connectors
GRI 6: rated voltage 48 V falls under 'For a voltage not exceeding 80 V'; the cable is of a kind used for telecommunications (data transmission), 8544.49.10.00

rejected_alternatives.reason: for conductors rated over 80 V up to 1,000 V (N357575 LAN cable was rated 300 V); this cable is rated 48 V
'Other' at 80 V or less; this cable is of a kind used for telecommunications
cable is not fitted with connectors

missing_facts: Confirm the 48 V rating is the maximum rated voltage (Cat6 cables are often rated 300 V, which would give 8544.49.30.80)
classification.rationale: The Cat6 cable is an insulated copper electric conductor of heading 8544, rated under 1,000 V and not fitted with connectors, so it falls in 8544.49. CBP rulings on the same kind of LAN cable (e.g., NY N357575) used 8544.49.3080 because those cables were rated 300 V; here the stated rated voltage is 48 V, which places the cable in the 'not exceeding 80 V' group. Because it carries data in network cabling, it is of a kind used for telecommunications, 8544.49.10.00.
